newsitem.title: USA: Input/Output posts sharp gains, tops volume.
newsitem.headline: Input/Output posts sharp gains, tops volume.

text.p: Seismic survey company Input/Output Inc posted sharp gains on the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday despite a downgrade from Robinson-Humphrey Co.
Shares of the Stafford, Texas, company rose 2-5/8, or more than 16 percent, to 18-3/4 in late afternoon trade. Volume was 6.9 million shares, tops among NYSE companies.
The shares dropped 7-1/2 to 16-3/8 on Wednesday after the company announced a second-quarter earnings forecast that was worse than expected.
Asked about Thursday's rise, one trader said, "Did you see what it did yesterday? It was a 30 percent drop -- that's just an overreaction."
Robinson-Humphrey cut its rating for Input/Output to long-term buy from short-term buy on Wednesday. A spokesman for the Atlanta firm said it was reviewing its earnings forecasts.

Milwaukee's Robert W. Baird said it had cut its earnings forecast for Input/Output. The earnings per share (EPS) estimate for fiscal 1997 was cut to $0.87 from $1.20, and the EPS estimate for fiscal 1998 was trimmed to $1.30 from $1.60.
